title: Why do earthquakes happen?
examples: How do we know where the plates are moving?
What is the difference between a fault and a plate boundary?

explain.say: The Earth's surface is not one solid piece you know.
These large pieces are called tectonic plates moving slowly.
When plates push past each other they create lines called faults.
Stress builds up until the rocks suddenly slip along the fault line.
Scientists measure earthquake size using scales like the Richter scale.
In real life, when we see a large earthquake we know plates moved.

faq.q: Are all earthquakes caused by plate movement?
faq.a: Most large earthquakes happen where tectonic plates meet or slide past. Sometimes smaller ones can happen for other reasons too.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fault and a plate boundary?
faq.a: A plate boundary is where two large plates meet. A fault is a crack or break within the ground itself.

faq.q: How do scientists measure how big an earthquake is?
faq.a: They use scales like the Richter scale or the moment magnitude scale. These measure the energy released by the shaking.
asks: Can you measure the quake size?

faq.q: Does the size of the earthquake tell us how deep it was?
faq.a: The scale measures the energy released, not the depth. Earthquakes can happen at many depths underground.
asks: Is depth important for the scale?

faq.q: Can we predict when the next earthquake will happen?
faq.a: Currently, scientists cannot predict the exact time or place of the next earthquake. They can only predict where they might happen.
asks: Will we know when it happens?
Can you tell me the date?

facts: The Earth is broken into several large pieces called tectonic plates.
These plates float and move very slowly on the Earth's mantle.
Friction builds up along faults where plates meet.
An earthquake happens when the stored energy suddenly releases.

quiz.why: The build-up of stress along a fault line finally overcomes the friction, causing a sudden slip and releasing energy.

wrong.0: This movement is constant and does not build up enough stress to cause a sudden break.
wrong.1: While magma movement is related, the main trigger for shaking is the sudden release of stored stress on the crust.
wrong.2: Ocean water movement is not the direct cause of the ground shaking from tectonic forces.

wrong.0: The scale measures the size of the event, not the duration of the shaking.
wrong.1: The scale is a measure of energy, not a direct measurement of plate distance moved.
wrong.3: The scale measures energy, not the depth of the earthquake underground.

quiz.say: Which feature is the area where the plates meet?
quiz.why: The plate boundary is the general location where the large tectonic plates interact and cause stress.

wrong.0: A seismic wave is the energy that travels after the movement, not the location of the movement.
wrong.2: A fault is a crack, but the boundary is the larger zone where the plates interact.
wrong.3: The mantle is the layer beneath the plates, not the meeting line itself.
